findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author link
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness for the light-theme (first) argument and uses the complement (100% - X) for the dark-theme argument, i.e. this should be `(30%, 70%)`. As written, the author name in "in reply to" expansions becomes much lighter (lower contrast) on light themes — an unintended visual regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix.

findings.title: Arguments appear swapped for .custom-message-length, darkening light themes
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch dropped from 70% to 30%, making this hint text substantially darker on light themes, and it diverges from the desktop rule (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which uses `(70%, 30%)`. The two arguments look swapped; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed 20% -> 50%
findings.body: In `.topic-map h3` the original value `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value is now 50% instead of 20%, so the topic map heading loses contrast on light themes, and it no longer matches the desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321) which uses `(20%, 80%)`. Expected conversion: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the group member name on existing light themes. If only the dark-theme behaviour was meant to change, this should be `(30%, 70%)`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop stylesheet: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, altering the light-theme rendering (lighter, lower contrast) in addition to the intended dark-theme fix. Expected `(30%, 70%)` to preserve existing light-theme output.

findings.title: #file-uploading still uses scale-color($secondary) for both themes
findings.body: `#file-uploading { color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%); }` was left unconverted while the adjacent `#draft-status` on line 36 was fixed. On a light theme `$secondary` is white, so scaling it 50% toward white yields a near-white color drawn on `#reply-control`'s light-gray background (`dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, 90%, -60%)`), making the upload status text effectively unreadable. It should use `dark-light-choose(...)` with `$primary`-derived color for light themes, like the other rules in this PR.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification color still scale-color($primary)
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in a file that this PR otherwise converted. On dark themes this lightens `$primary` (already light) toward white, producing a near-white count badge instead of the intended muted gray, which is exactly the problem the PR fixes elsewhere. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` for consistency.

findings.title: Comment documenting topic-list default color is now stale
findings.body: The comment `// is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` above the coldmap rules describes the default topic-list cell color, but those defaults were changed in this PR (`common/base/_topic-list.scss` now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`). The comment should be updated so future readers don't copy the obsolete single-argument form.
